irac.issue: Whether the adopted son can divest an estate that had devolved by inheritance from a collateral prior to the date of adoption.
irac.rule: The principle of relation back applies only when the claim of the adopted son relates to the estate of the adoptive father. Where succession to the properties of a person other than an adoptive father is involved, the principle applicable is that inheritance once vested cannot be divested.
irac.application: The court applied the rule that inheritance once vested cannot be divested to the case where the adopted son's claim relates to the estate of a collateral, and held that the adopted son cannot divest the estate that had devolved by inheritance from a collateral prior to the date of adoption.
irac.conclusion: The court overruled the decision in Anant Bhikappa Patil (Minor) v. Shankar Ramchandra Patil and held that an adopted son's right to divest an estate does not extend to estates inherited by the adoptive father from collaterals before the adoption.
